title: Swampland correspondence: the electromagnetic coupling and the Emergence Proposal
html:
Remark. Swampland correspondence: the electromagnetic coupling and the Emergence Proposal

The electromagnetic coupling is not a free input. It is a categorical trace ratio,

  \alpha_{EM} = \frac{h^{2}}{q\,\delta_q(T_{2,9})\,\delta_q(T_{3,5})}.

This exact algebraic identity in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] is built from the two genus-4-saturating force-carrier torus knots. It echoes the Emergence Proposal.

The Swampland statement. Gauge couplings and kinetic terms are not fundamental. They are generated in the infrared by integrating out a tower of charged states. Weak coupling emerges at large distance in moduli space [heidenreich2018, ooguri-vafa2007].

QOU translation. The discrete topological data of the force-carrier knots generates the coupling, replacing a continuum loop sum. The conclusion remains parallel. The coupling \alpha_{EM} is a derived consequence of the substrate. Sending the coupling toward its classical limit forces q \to 1. Here, the skein parameter h = q - q^{-1} vanishes. The braiding degenerates to a symmetric monoidal structure. The topological information distinguishing charged states is erased. This forms the QOU image of weak coupling at the boundary of the parameter space.

Scope. The trace-ratio identity and its combinatorial form \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q are proved. Agreement with the measured value at the substrate parameter is leading-order. The remaining high-precision residual awaits a separate Chern–Simons correction. The emergence described here is a structural fact: topology fixes the coupling. This is not a claim that its measured value is fully derived.
